seoTitle: How to Get Multiple Stripe Accounts With One LLC
metaDescription: Learn how to add extra Stripe accounts under a single LLC, keep payouts and API keys organized, and avoid mistakes that trigger account restrictions.
intro: Running several brands or stores under one legal entity doesn't mean you're stuck with a single Stripe account. This guide explains how to add additional accounts linked to the same LLC, what business and banking information you'll need, and best practices for keeping payouts, transactions, and API keys separated per store.

steps.heading: Gather the requirements for an extra account
steps.body: Before adding a new account, make sure you have the business and banking details Stripe will ask for, since incomplete information is a common cause of delays.

steps.heading: Add a new account from your Stripe dashboard
steps.body: Stripe allows multiple accounts tied to the same business entity, and you can add them from within your existing dashboard.

steps.heading: Manage payouts and API keys separately
steps.body: Keep each account's payouts and API keys distinct so transactions from different stores don't get mixed up or misattributed.

steps.heading: Follow best practices to avoid restrictions
steps.body: Stripe monitors for unusual account patterns, so following their policies closely when setting up multiple accounts helps you avoid holds or restrictions.

faq.question: Can I really have more than one Stripe account under a single LLC?
faq.answer: Yes, Stripe allows multiple accounts linked to the same registered business entity, which is useful for owners managing several brands or stores.

faq.question: Do I need separate banking details for each Stripe account?
faq.answer: You'll want to review Stripe's requirements per account, and keeping payouts organized separately per store is recommended even if some banking details overlap.

faq.question: What causes Stripe to restrict multiple accounts?
faq.answer: Restrictions often stem from mismatched business information or patterns that look inconsistent across accounts, so accuracy and consistency matter.

faq.question: Who is this setup useful for?
faq.answer: It's aimed at e-commerce owners, agency owners, and anyone running multiple online ventures under one company.
